Interfaces: Produce PROTOCOL=1, RUN_FORMAT=1; validate_record(kind: str, value: dict) -> dict; atomic_json(path: Path, value: dict) -> None; Journal(root: Path).append(kind: str, data: dict) -> dict and .replay(after: int) -> list[dict]. Produce ActivityBarrier with try_enter(kind: str, *, control: bool=False) -> context-manager-or-None, close(generation: int) -> None, seal(generation: int) -> None, reopen(generation: int) -> None, snapshot() -> dict. A returned section counts immediately, before __enter__; __exit__ always releases. Snapshot has generation, closed, sealed, active_sections and counts by kind. close denies work; counted control=True sections may enter until seal denies all admission. Matching reopen unseals. Admission close and section acquisition share one mutex. The module runs standalone with only stdlib imports.

Work: Implement the protocol records and enums from the design, strict full lowercase 40-hex SHAs and increasing generations/sequences. Journal append uses one immutable sequence file per event before replacing state; recover a complete journal record whose state update was interrupted. Exclude partial files, detect gaps/corruption, and block unknown versions. Child and parent writers never overwrite each other's records. Atomic writes flush and fsync before replace. An installer-supplied state root carries owner ACLs; never log secrets. A stale generation cannot reopen a current barrier. This foundational module must import without FastAPI or the drover package. Validate request.operation_id/generation/instance, command.operation_id and child.operation_id/ledger_schema, enrollment/release ledger_schema and required_schema (both required, strictly non-negative integers, equal within each record) and healthy receipt manifest_digest. Require UUID identity fields, non-negative integer generations/schema (reject booleans); child schema alone may be null before preflight/on read failure. Cancel/retry require non-null operation ID. Define handoff_schema with operation/generation/instance/creation identity/schema/challenge/sequence as in the worked example; null when no planned handoff. Preserve observed identities exactly, including the request identity preceding the new parent-assigned operation.

Regression coverage: Test enrollment/release required_schema: missing, bool, negative or unequal actual/required values reject; valid matching pairs round-trip. Schema-field excerpts are not complete records; validate the full state and child examples with complete fixture enrollment/manifest.

Verification: run the focused test tests.test_reload_protocol using the preinstalled interpreter; new platform-independent tests must execute, not skip. Required Windows-only checks need an authorized Windows worker and an actual passing receipt. See the implementation plan task #0 for test steps.
acceptance: Barrier close races atomically with acquisition; an already acquired section can finish, and all later acquisition is denied until matching reopen.
Torn state after durable journal append replays exactly once; malformed/gapped/unknown-version data fails closed without changing active SHA.
Record validation covers every field in the spec worked example; journal event IDs support transactional ledger mirroring deduplication.

Requests preserve observed operation_id/generation/instance; missing/malformed fields and null cancel/retry operation fail validation; child status requires ledger_schema (null is explicit non-ready, bool/negative invalid). Both worked JSON records validate.

Enrollment/release ledger_schema and independently established required_schema are mandatory, strict integer matching pairs; healthy manifest_digest and handoff_schema round-trip without inventing live evidence.

Test enrollment/release required_schema: missing, bool, negative or unequal actual/required values reject; valid matching pairs round-trip. Schema-field excerpts are not complete records; validate the full state and child examples with complete fixture enrollment/manifest.

Interfaces: Consume protocol records. Produce transition(state: dict, event: dict, now: float) -> tuple[dict, list[dict]]: a pure reducer returning next state and ordered effect descriptions. Effects use {kind,data}; kinds are stage, command, spawn, probe, terminate_validation_pid, bridge_start, bridge_stop, latch, notify. Stable supervisor owns execution; no process, filesystem or SQLite access in reducer.

Work: Define idle/pending/draining/stopping/validating/committed and blocked/rolling_back/rolled_back/failed transitions exactly as the design. Coalesce newest descendant before draining only; pin target thereafter. Drain timeout 900s blocks without kill, shutdown timeout 30s blocks, readiness timeout 60s includes 15 stable advancing-heartbeat seconds, failed validation shutdown grace 10s. One fallback only; two attempts per ten minutes including fallback, persisted failed latch survives scheduled-task relaunch. Only healthy candidate commit changes active/previous. Fallback disables auto and keeps admission closed; cancel then explicitly resumes it. Distinguish intentional exit 75, owner stop, unexpected exit and identity uncertainty. Stale events cannot change state. Request events retain their observed operation_id/generation/instance. Compare them atomically with current state before any effect; reject stale tuples or disallowed phases, journal control_rejected and preserve phase/barrier/auto. Check stored key/payload/result before identity comparison: exact duplicates return the prior result without effects; key reuse with changed payload conflicts. For each new reload/stop or retry consume a parent-generated event.new_operation_id UUID (journaled before reducer application, making replay deterministic), retire the old ID even when SHA/PID is unchanged, and advance generation for a new drain/retry; fallback retains operation ID but advances generation/instance. Propagate identities through commands, child status and journal. Require schema-match/freshness evidence before drain/stopping/readiness; expired handoff permission or unexpected exit selects retained recovery, never an unfenced candidate spawn.

Verification: run the focused test tests.test_reload_machine using the preinstalled interpreter; new platform-independent tests must execute, not skip. Required Windows-only checks need an authorized Windows worker and an actual passing receipt. See the implementation plan task #2 for test steps.
acceptance: A failed candidate selects A once while main/ledger effects are absent; a failed fallback latches and restart cannot clear the latch.
Drain/shutdown timeout effects never include termination; only a proven validation-only PID may request bounded termination.
Auto off before drain cancels automatic work; after drain it never tears down the handoff; owner preference updates are preserved.

Delayed cancel/retry targeting retired X cannot change phase/admission/auto or emit work commands for Y draining the same SHA, including after replay; operation, generation and instance mismatches each reject independently.

Exact duplicate controls return prior result without reapplying; changed payload under one key conflicts. Missing/mismatched schema or expired handoff proof cannot authorize candidate drain/commit/spawn.
